newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March industrial price index rises 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada March industrial price index rises 0.2 pct.

text.p: Statistics Canada on Friday issued the following economic indicators for March.
INDUSTRIAL PRODUCT PRICE INDEX Month-on-Month Year-on- Year
INDUSTRIAL PRODUCT PRICE INDEX Month-on-Month Year-on- Year
The IPPI reflects the prices producers receive as goods leave their plants.
Statistics Canada said the 0.9 percent increase in the 12- month level was due more to the decline of prices in early 1996 than to the rise in prices in early 1997.

The federal agency said exchange rate movement dominated the month-to-month change in industrial prices. The March increase in the value of the U.S. dollar against the Canadian dollar raised the value in Canadian dollars of all export prices quoted in U.S. currency. This increased the month-to- month change in industrial prices from zero in February to 0.2 percent in March, StatsCan said.
The agency said the impact was most noticeable for motor vehicles, pulp, paper and wood products.

In March, the most important monthly price increases were for non-ferrous metal products, motor vehicles and feeds using oilseed products, the agency said. Petroleum products prices offset most of these increases.
